questions.question: A circular track has radius 35 m. A runner does 5 rounds. Distance run (π = 22/7) =
questions.explanation: Circumference = 2πr = 2×(22/7)×35 = 220 m per round. 5 rounds = 5×220 = 1,100 m.

questions.explanation: Circumference = 2πr = 2×(22/7)×1.4 = 8.8 m per rotation. 100 rotations = 100×8.8 = 880 m.

questions.question: Two circles: Circle A (radius 7 cm) and Circle B (radius 14 cm). Ratio of their areas A : B =
questions.explanation: A(A) = π×49; A(B) = π×196. Ratio = 49 : 196 = 1 : 4. Area ratio = (ratio of radii)² = (7/14)² = (1/2)² = 1/4.

questions.question: A square park (side 28 m) has a circular fountain (radius 7 m) in the centre. Area of the park NOT covered by the fountain (π = 22/7) =
questions.explanation: Square area = 28² = 784 m². Circular fountain = π×7² = (22/7)×49 = 154 m². Remaining = 784−154 = 630 m².

questions.question: A cow is tied to a post with a rope of 7 m. The maximum area of grass the cow can graze (π = 22/7) =
questions.explanation: The cow can graze in a circle of radius 7 m. Area = πr² = (22/7)×49 = 154 m².

questions.question: A circular pond of diameter 14 m is surrounded by a path 7 m wide. Area of path only (π = 22/7) =
questions.explanation: Inner radius = 7 m. Outer radius = 7+7 = 14 m. Path = π(R²−r²) = (22/7)(196−49) = (22/7)×147 = 22×21 = 462 m².

A wire 176 cm long is bent first into a circle, then straightened and bent into a square. Which has the greater area?
questions.explanation: Circle: C=176 → r=176/(2π)=176×7/44=28 cm. Area=π×28²=(22/7)×784=2,464 cm². Square: side=176/4=44 cm. Area=44²=1,936 cm². Circle > Square. (For same perimeter, circle always has greatest area.)

The ratio of circumference to diameter of any circle is:
questions.explanation: C/d = π for any circle (this is the definition of π). C = πd = 2πr. π is an irrational number ≈ 3.14159... We use 22/7 as a close approximation. This ratio is constant for ALL circles.
